about:
# JunkMate

Sells your junk and repairs your gear whenever you open a vendor. An addon for World of Warcraft: Forever (client 1.60.x).

Formerly called VendorMate. It was renamed in 0.3.0 because a Retail addon called VendorMate is already on CurseForge. Type `/junkmate` now.

## What it does

Every time you open a vendor window, JunkMate:

- **sells the junk** in your bags (the grey items the game's own "Sell All Junk" button would sell), and
- **repairs your gear**, if the vendor can and you can afford it,

then tells you in chat what that earned and cost, for example:

> Sold 7 junk items for 12s 50c. Repaired for 34s.

Hold **Shift** while opening a vendor to skip both that time.

It also **warns you when your gear is wearing out**. While your most worn piece is below 25% durability, a line stays on screen ("Gear worn: 18% left"), with one line in chat when it first drops below. It clears once you repair. A blacksmith's hammer also pulses on JunkMate's minimap button; click it and the top of the window names the worn piece. You can drag the line to wherever you like, and set the level to 10%, 25% or 50%.

While your gear is worn it also **helps you find a repairer**: the minimap's own repair tracking is switched on (where the game has it), the worn-gear line names the nearest repairer you've used, with the distance ("Nearest repair: William MacGregor, 180 yd"; click it for a map pin), and a known repairer's tooltip says they repair. JunkMate learns each repairer when you open their shop.

Whenever you carry junk it would sell, **a gold coin shows on the minimap button**. Hover the button for what the junk is worth and the nearest vendor you've used ("Nearest vendor: Mike Miller, 120 yd"); right-click it for a map pin on them. A known vendor's tooltip says they'll buy it. While you have junk, vendors also show on the minimap: the game's own vendor tracking is switched on (food and drink, reagents, repair), and every vendor you've used gets a gold coin. JunkMate learns each vendor when you open their shop.

It also **warns you when your bags are nearly full**. Down to your last 4 slots, the minimap button shows how many are left (a yellow number) and chat says so; once the bags are full it shows a flashing red **!**. Set it to 2, 4 or 8 free slots. Only ordinary bags count, not herb, mining or other special bags.

**Makes room for loot.** When something won't fit in your bags, JunkMate first **restacks** them, putting partial stacks together, which loses nothing. If that doesn't free a slot, a small window offers to destroy the cheapest thing you don't need, so the loot fits:

> Destroy [Broken Fang] (worth 5c)? To make room for [Green Bracers].

The window opens on the left of the screen, above the chat, so it never covers the middle; drag it wherever you like. During a fight it stays hidden and comes back once the fight is over, except for **quest items**: if one won't fit mid-fight, the window shows at once so you can grab it and run. In a fight the controller's A button can't be borrowed, so click Destroy, or set the key binding (Key Bindings > AddOns > JunkMate > "Make room: destroy the offered item").

**Nothing is ever destroyed until you press Destroy.** Then the loot is picked up for you. Press **Not this one** to see the next choice, or **Keep always** so JunkMate never offers that item again.

- **What it offers, in order:** grey items first, then food and drink you've outgrown, then gear that isn't an upgrade for your class (wrong armour type, or a lower item level than what you wear), cheapest first.
- **What it never offers:** gear in an equipment set, gear with a special effect or resistances (Riding Gloves, a fishing hat, fire-resistance gear), bind-on-equip greens and better (worth more at the auction house), quest items, crafting materials, recipes, profession tools (skinning knife, mining pick, fishing poles, enchanting rods and so on), the hearthstone, soul shards and class reagents, keys, bags, ammo, potions and other consumables, gear that would be an upgrade, anything epic, buff food ("well fed"), and the **best food and drink you carry for your level**. So only the old stacks of apples and bread go, never what you'd actually eat.
- **Worth it or not:** it only makes room for quest items, crafting materials, anything green or better, upgrades, or loot worth more than what would go. A 1-copper pebble won't cost you anything.

**Quest rewards too:** if your bags are too full for a quest's reward, JunkMate makes room the same way, then hands the quest in for you (or tells you to talk to the quest giver again). It never chooses a reward for you.

**Opens clams and the like.** When your bags get down to the warning level, JunkMate opens clams and other "Right Click to Open" items and takes what's inside, which frees slots (nine clams become one stack of meat). Never in a fight, and never with a vendor, bank, mailbox, trade or auction window open, where opening would sell or move the item instead. Locked boxes are left alone. `/junkmate open` does it now.

JunkMate also **restacks on its own** when your bags get down to the warning level, before warning you.

**Tidies the bank.** When you open your bank, JunkMate puts the bank's partial stacks together, then tops up its partial stacks of crafting materials from your bags (15 Linen Cloth in the bank and 7 in your bags: 5 go in to make 20, and 2 stay with you), and says in chat what it did. Only crafting materials move, and only onto stacks already in the bank, so the food, potions, ammo and reagents you carry stay with you and nothing lands in an empty bank slot. Hold **Shift** while opening the bank to skip it.

**Sells more than junk.** At a vendor, after the grey items, JunkMate also sells food and drink you've outgrown and gear your class can't use (at most 12 a visit, so everything can still be bought back). Gear you can wear but isn't an upgrade is never sold.

**Tooltips say what JunkMate does with an item.** Hover anything in your bags to see whether JunkMate keeps it and why ("JunkMate keeps this: in an equipment set"), or where it stands ("JunkMate: sold at vendors; 1st to go if your bags fill").

**Vendor prices on tooltips:** hover over any item to see what it sells for at a vendor, and for a stack what the whole stack is worth ("Vendor: 13c each, 20 for 2s 60c"). Items a vendor will not buy say so. Handy for deciding what to vendor, auction or mail to your bank alt. Forever's own tooltip already shows the sell price of the whole stack; there JunkMate adds only what one is worth ("Sell price each: 3c"), for stacks.

## Options

Type `/junkmate` (or `/jmate`) to open the options, click JunkMate's minimap button (drag it to move it), or use the addon's entry in the minimap's addon list. The top of the window always shows your gear's condition and your bags' free slots.

| Setting | Command |
|---|---|
| Sell junk when a vendor opens | `/junkmate junk` |
| Repair when a vendor who can opens | `/junkmate repair` |
| Say in chat what was sold and repaired | `/junkmate report` |
| Warn on screen when gear is wearing out | `/junkmate worn` |
| Warn when your bags are nearly full | `/junkmate bags` |
| Vendor prices on item tooltips | `/junkmate price` |
| Show the minimap button | `/junkmate button` |
| Offer to make room when loot won't fit | (options window) |
| Restack when bags get nearly full | (options window) |
| Tidy the bank when it opens | (options window), or `/junkmate bank` to run it now |
| Also sell outgrown food and gear you can't use | (options window) |
| Say on tooltips what JunkMate does with an item | (options window) |

Also: `/junkmate room` (make room now, without loot), `/junkmate restack` (restack now), `/junkmate keep` (what it never offers; `/junkmate keep clear` empties it) and `/junkmate destroyed` (what was destroyed this session).

## Good to know

- Only junk is sold: grey items. Nothing white or better is ever sold.
- A destroyed item is gone for good. That is why JunkMate never destroys anything without you pressing the button, and says in chat what went.
- A mistaken sale can be bought back from the vendor's Buyback tab, as usual.
- Repairs are paid from your own money, never a guild bank.

## Controller

With a game controller, the **B** button closes the JunkMate window, like the X and Escape do. In the make-room window, **Y** destroys, the **right shoulder** shows the next choice and the **left shoulder** keeps the item always, so A and X keep their jobs in the loot window. While a window is open, B closes it; once it is closed, B goes back to whatever you have it set to. When a fight starts, B goes straight back to its usual job, even with the window open.

## More from this author

Other small addons for World of Warcraft: Forever, all free:

- **[GatherLog](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gatherlog)** remembers ore, herbs, fishing pools, skinning spots, chests and rares across all your characters, and guides you back to the best spots.
- **[MouseTip](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/mousetip)** shows tooltips at your mouse cursor.
- **[RangeShade](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/rangeshade)** shades action buttons red when your target is out of range.
- **[AltGlance](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/altglance)** shows all your characters at a glance: level, gold, rested and where you left them.
- **[SwiftQuest](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/swiftquest)** accepts quests and hands them in as soon as you talk to the quest giver, without ever choosing a reward for you.
- **[SessionRecap](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/sessionrecap)** keeps a running tally of your play session: gold, experience per hour, quests, gathering and loot.
- **[MacroKit](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/macrokit)** adds ready-made macros for your class and spec, for all nine classes, and never overwrites your own.
- **[ZoomPad](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/zoompad)** puts big + and - buttons on screen that zoom the camera, made for the Steam Deck touchscreen.
- **[GamepadMacros](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gamepadmacros)** adds ready-made macros for controller and Steam Deck players: heal yourself, use a quest item, save and wear gear, leave a group, emotes.
- **[FDR - Flight Data Recorder](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/fdr-flight-data-recorder)** times every flight-master flight and counts your next one down to landing.

## Installing

Install it from [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/junkmate) with the CurseForge app, or by hand: copy this folder into `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\` as `JunkMate`, restart the game, and enable JunkMate on the character select screen.

## Developing

- `tools\Link-Addon.ps1` links this folder into the game's AddOns folder, so edits are live after `/reload`.
- `python tests/run.py` runs the tests (`pip install lupa` once). They run the addon in real Lua 5.1 against a fake of the game's API.
- `tools\Publish.ps1 -Message "..."` runs the tests and pushes to GitHub. GitHub runs the tests again on every push.

## Releasing

`tools\Publish.ps1 -Message "Release x.y.z" -Tag vx.y.z` publishes and tags. The tag makes GitHub package the addon and attach the zip to a GitHub release.

To also upload to CurseForge and Wago, two things are needed once:

1. Create the project on each site, then add its ID to `JunkMate.toc`:
   `## X-Curse-Project-ID: 123456` and `## X-Wago-ID: abc123`.
2. Create an upload token on each site and add it to this repository's secrets (Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions) as `CF_API_KEY` and `WAGO_API_TOKEN`.

Before each release: raise `## Version:` in `JunkMate.toc` and add the version to `CHANGELOG.md`.

# JunkMate

## 0.20.1

- **Fixed: the vendor map pin wasn't cleared after selling your junk.** The game stores a pin's position slightly rounded, so JunkMate didn't recognise the pin as its own any more and left it alone (as it does with pins you place yourself). It now remembers where the game actually put it. A pin left over from before can be removed with `/junkmate unpin`.

## 0.20.0

- **Destroy all greys in one press:** when you have two or more grey items, the make-room window adds a button for all of them at once (*"Destroy all 4 grey items (worth 23c)"*; D-pad up on a controller), so one press frees several slots instead of one window per item.
- **Help before the bags are full:** the "Only 2 bag slots left" line now says what would go next (*"Next to go: Broken Fang (5c)"*) and offers to destroy every grey item now.
- **Make room anyway:** when the loot is worth less than anything JunkMate would destroy, the chat line now offers to make room anyway. `/junkmate room` always does, and `/junkmate greys` offers every grey item.
- Those offers are clickable links where the game allows addon links; otherwise the line names the command to type.

## 0.19.0

The make-room window, from the user-experience review:

- **Controller buttons no longer clash with the loot window.** The loot window uses A (loot), X (loot all) and B (close), so pressing A to loot used to destroy an item instead. Now **Y destroys**, the **right shoulder** skips to the next item and the **left shoulder** keeps it always; A and X are the loot window's again. B still closes the make-room window first.
- **The buttons are dimmed while presses don't count yet** (the short pause after the window appears), and light up when they do, so a press is never silently ignored.
- **It opens beside the loot window** while that's open (or beside the quest window, for a quest reward), so it's where you're already looking. If you've dragged it somewhere yourself, it opens there instead.

## 0.18.1

- **Removing the map pin:** with a controller the world map offers no way to remove a pin, so JunkMate adds one: type `/junkmate unpin`, or set the key binding *Key Bindings > AddOns > JunkMate > Remove the map pin* (a controller button works). It removes any map pin, and JunkMate's vendor pin then stays off until the next time you have junk.

## 0.18.0

- **A map pin on the nearest vendor, all by itself:** while you carry junk, the map pin and its arrow sit on the nearest vendor JunkMate knows. It moves when a closer one is nearer, and it's cleared once there's nothing left to sell.
- A map pin you placed yourself is never moved or removed. If you remove JunkMate's pin, it isn't put back on that vendor until the next time you have junk.
- The junk line on screen now just says what your junk is worth, without the vendor's name. The option is now called "Pin the nearest vendor when you have junk".

## 0.17.2

- **Says when it learns a vendor:** the first time any of your characters learns one, by opening their shop or by hovering or targeting them, chat says *"Learned a vendor: Christopher Hewen. All your characters will know them now."* Vendors it already knows stay quiet. (Opening a shop has always taught JunkMate, silently, since 0.14.0.)

## 0.17.1

- **Learning vendors on clients that won't say how far away an NPC is:** targeting a vendor now teaches JunkMate even then (hovering still needs the distance). New: `/junkmate learn` tries to learn your target and says why if it can't.
- The minimap coins no longer depend on one map function some clients may not have.

## 0.17.0

- **Learns vendors without a visit:** hover over or target an NPC close by (within about 10 yards) whose title says they sell things (*General Trade Goods Vendor*, *Bowyer*, *Trade Supplies*, *Innkeeper* and so on), and JunkMate remembers them as a vendor: a gold coin on the minimap while you have junk, and a candidate for "Nearest vendor". Walking through a town fills them in. Trainers, guards, bankers and flight and stable masters are left out.
- The game doesn't tell addons where an NPC stands, so a vendor is learned at your own position, which is why only close ones count. A vendor whose shop you've opened keeps its exact spot.
- The title words are English, so on other languages' clients only opening a shop teaches JunkMate.

## 0.16.0

- **Vendors on the minimap, only while you have junk to sell:**
  - JunkMate switches on the minimap's own vendor tracking (Food & Drink, Reagents and Repair, whichever the game has), so vendors nearby show even if you've never used them, and switches it off again once there's nothing left to sell. Tracking you switched on yourself is left alone.
  - Every vendor you've used gets a gold coin on the minimap while it's in view. Hover a coin for who it is and what they'd pay for your junk.
- Switch it off in the options: "Show vendors on the minimap when you have junk", under *At a vendor*.

## 0.15.1

- **The junk-to-sell line on screen is back, as an option** (off unless you switch it on): "Show the junk-to-sell line on screen" under *At a vendor*, or `/junkmate junkbanner`. It says what your junk is worth and names the nearest vendor; click it for a map pin, drag it to move it, and `/junkmate junkbanner reset` puts it back. The coin on the minimap button shows junk either way.

## 0.15.0

- **The options window is in two columns under headings** (At a vendor, Worn gear, Bags, Tooltips and minimap), about half as tall, so it fits small screens like the Legion Go.
- **The worn-gear line on screen has its own switch** ("Show the worn-gear line on screen", or `/junkmate banner`). With it off, the hammer on the minimap button and the chat line still warn you.
- **Moving it:** hover the line for how; drag it anywhere and it stays there. `/junkmate banner reset` puts it back at the top of the screen.

## 0.14.2

- **No more "Junk to sell" banner on screen:** the gold coin on the minimap button says it instead. Hover the button for what the junk is worth and the nearest vendor you've used; **right-click** it for a map pin on that vendor. Known vendors still say on their tooltip that they'll buy your junk.

## 0.14.1

- **A gold coin on the minimap button** while you carry junk JunkMate would sell, in the bottom-right corner (the hammer for worn gear stays bottom-left, the bag count top-right). Hover the button to see how many items and what they're worth.

## 0.14.0

Finding a vendor whenever you have junk to sell, the way 0.13.0 finds a repairer:

- **A line on screen** while you carry anything JunkMate would sell (grey items, plus outgrown food and gear you can't use if that's switched on) says what it's worth and names the nearest vendor you've used, with the distance kept up to date: *"Junk to sell: 6 items (1s 20c)  Nearest vendor: Mike Miller, 120 yd"*. Click it for a map pin and the arrow; drag it to move it. It goes away at a vendor, and once there's nothing left to sell.
- **Known vendors say so:** their tooltip says *"JunkMate: buys your junk (6 items, 1s 20c)"*, and targeting one says so in chat (once a minute at most).
- JunkMate now remembers every vendor whose shop you open, not just repairers. `/junkmate vendor` names the nearest one and pins it. Switch it all off in the options ("Point to a vendor when you have junk").

## 0.13.0

  - Every vendor you've used gets a gold coin on the minimap while it's in view. Hover a coin for who it is and what they'd pay for your junk.
- Switch it off in the options: "Show vendors on the minimap when you have junk", under *At a vendor*.

## 0.15.1

- **The junk-to-sell line on screen is back, as an option** (off unless you switch it on): "Show the junk-to-sell line on screen" under *At a vendor*, or `/junkmate junkbanner`. It says what your junk is worth and names the nearest vendor; click it for a map pin, drag it to move it, and `/junkmate junkbanner reset` puts it back. The coin on the minimap button shows junk either way.

## 0.15.0

- **The options window is in two columns under headings** (At a vendor, Worn gear, Bags, Tooltips and minimap), about half as tall, so it fits small screens like the Legion Go.

## 0.14.2

- **No more "Junk to sell" banner on screen:** the gold coin on the minimap button says it instead. Hover the button for what the junk is worth and the nearest vendor you've used; **right-click** it for a map pin on that vendor. Known vendors still say on their tooltip that they'll buy your junk.

## 0.14.1

- **A gold coin on the minimap button** while you carry junk JunkMate would sell, in the bottom-right corner (the hammer for worn gear stays bottom-left, the bag count top-right). Hover the button to see how many items and what they're worth.

## 0.14.0

Finding a vendor whenever you have junk to sell, the way 0.13.0 finds a repairer:

- **A line on screen** while you carry anything JunkMate would sell (grey items, plus outgrown food and gear you can't use if that's switched on) says what it's worth and names the nearest vendor you've used, with the distance kept up to date: *"Junk to sell: 6 items (1s 20c)  Nearest vendor: Mike Miller, 120 yd"*. Click it for a map pin and the arrow; drag it to move it. It goes away at a vendor, and once there's nothing left to sell.
- **Known vendors say so:** their tooltip says *"JunkMate: buys your junk (6 items, 1s 20c)"*, and targeting one says so in chat (once a minute at most).
- JunkMate now remembers every vendor whose shop you open, not just repairers. `/junkmate vendor` names the nearest one and pins it. Switch it all off in the options ("Point to a vendor when you have junk").

## 0.13.0

Finding a repairer while your gear is worn:

- **Minimap repair tracking:** while your gear is worn, JunkMate switches on the minimap's own "Repair" tracking (where the game has it), so repairers show on the minimap, and switches it off again once you've repaired. If you had it on yourself, it's left on.
- **The nearest repairer you've used:** JunkMate remembers every vendor who repairs when you open their shop. While your gear is worn, the worn-gear line names the nearest one, with the distance kept up to date as you move: *"Gear worn: 20% left  Nearest repair: William MacGregor, 180 yd"*. Click the line for a map pin and the arrow to them (drag it to move it, as before). `/junkmate repairer` does the same.
- **Known repairers say so:** their tooltip says *"JunkMate: repairs here"* (with your gear's condition while it's worn), and targeting one while your gear is worn says so in chat.
- The game doesn't tell addons which NPCs repair, so the last two only know repairers you've opened a shop with. Both can be switched off in the options.

## 0.12.0

- **The make-room window says why it picked that item,** and what would go next. JunkMate offers grey items first, then food and drink you have outgrown, then gear that is no upgrade, cheapest first; now it says so for the item on offer:
  - *"Why this one: it's grey junk; the cheapest of 4 grey items."*
  - *"Why this one: with no grey items to offer, it's food you've outgrown (level 5; you also carry level 15)."*
  - *"...it's no upgrade (item level 5; what you wear there is 12)"* or *"...your class can't use mail."*
  - *"Next in line: Torn Pelt (worth 50c)."*

## 0.11.0

# JunkMate

## 0.18.1

- **Removing the map pin:** with a controller the world map offers no way to remove a pin, so JunkMate adds one: type `/junkmate unpin`, or set the key binding *Key Bindings > AddOns > JunkMate > Remove the map pin* (a controller button works). It removes any map pin, and JunkMate's vendor pin then stays off until the next time you have junk.

## 0.18.0

- **A map pin on the nearest vendor, all by itself:** while you carry junk, the map pin and its arrow sit on the nearest vendor JunkMate knows. It moves when a closer one is nearer, and it's cleared once there's nothing left to sell.
- A map pin you placed yourself is never moved or removed. If you remove JunkMate's pin, it isn't put back on that vendor until the next time you have junk.
- The junk line on screen now just says what your junk is worth, without the vendor's name. The option is now called "Pin the nearest vendor when you have junk".

## 0.17.2

- **Says when it learns a vendor:** the first time any of your characters learns one, by opening their shop or by hovering or targeting them, chat says *"Learned a vendor: Christopher Hewen. All your characters will know them now."* Vendors it already knows stay quiet. (Opening a shop has always taught JunkMate, silently, since 0.14.0.)

## 0.17.1

- **Learning vendors on clients that won't say how far away an NPC is:** targeting a vendor now teaches JunkMate even then (hovering still needs the distance). New: `/junkmate learn` tries to learn your target and says why if it can't.
- The minimap coins no longer depend on one map function some clients may not have.

## 0.17.0

- **Learns vendors without a visit:** hover over or target an NPC close by (within about 10 yards) whose title says they sell things (*General Trade Goods Vendor*, *Bowyer*, *Trade Supplies*, *Innkeeper* and so on), and JunkMate remembers them as a vendor: a gold coin on the minimap while you have junk, and a candidate for "Nearest vendor". Walking through a town fills them in. Trainers, guards, bankers and flight and stable masters are left out.
- The game doesn't tell addons where an NPC stands, so a vendor is learned at your own position, which is why only close ones count. A vendor whose shop you've opened keeps its exact spot.
- The title words are English, so on other languages' clients only opening a shop teaches JunkMate.
